page: Vultr vx1-g-32c-128g is a general-purpose virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 32 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core on an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. It lacks local storage, utilizing a 1 GB network-attached storage volume, and does not include a dedicated GPU.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in memory operations and single-threaded tasks. The server achieves top-tier results in large-block memory write bandwidth and PassMark memory scores. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, also rank in the top tier. Multi-core performance and database operations score in the average range, likely influenced by the shared CPU allocation. However, the system demonstrates strong throughput in static web serving and Redis SET operations, alongside top-tier text generation speeds for small and medium language models.

The primary tradeoff of the vx1-g-32c-128g is its shared CPU architecture and minimal local storage, which may introduce performance variability under sustained multi-core loads and requires external storage solutions for data-heavy applications. Given these characteristics, the server is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-heavy workloads that do not require continuous dedicated CPU performance. It is suited for static web serving, caching layers, memory-bound data processing, and lightweight language model inference.
